articles.title: U11 Jets Triumph at Coalminers U11s Mixed Supercup
articles.excerpt: The U11 Jets secured victory at the Coalminers U11s mixed supercup held at Whitworth Academy, progressing through the group stage and winning the final against Blyth.
articles.content_html:
A team of young footballers, called the U11 Jets, participated in the Coalminers U11s mixed supercup at Whitworth Academy. They successfully navigated the group stage, demonstrating strong teamwork and skill.

In the semi-final, the Jets faced Silksworth in a closely contested match, which they won to advance to the final. Their performance showcased their determination and ability to perform under pressure.

The final saw the Jets compete against Blyth, where they emerged victorious, adding another trophy to their achievements. The team's success reflects their hard work and dedication throughout the tournament.

This victory is a significant milestone for the U11 Jets, highlighting their potential and promising future in youth football.

articles.title: Whitworth Community High School Thanks Parents for Attending Evening
articles.excerpt: Whitworth Community High School expressed gratitude to parents and carers who attended the recent parents' evening with their children.
articles.content_html:
Whitworth Community High School has thanked parents and carers for attending the recent parents' evening held earlier this week. The school expressed appreciation for the involvement of families in their children's education.

The event provided an opportunity for parents to engage with teachers and discuss their children's progress. Such evenings are important for fostering communication between home and school.

The school encourages ongoing participation from families to support student development and success. Events like these are vital for building strong relationships within the school community.

Whitworth Community High School continues to prioritise collaboration with parents to enhance the educational experience for all students.

articles.title: Volunteers raise £450 for Christian Aid at Whitworth Skyline Walk breakfast
articles.excerpt: Volunteers from Thrum Hall Methodist Church raised £450 for Christian Aid by serving breakfast to walkers during the Whitworth Skyline Walk.
articles.content_html:
A group of volunteers from Thrum Hall Methodist Church raised £450 for Christian Aid by providing breakfast for participants in the Whitworth Skyline Walk.

The volunteers set up a breakfast stall along the route of the annual event, serving bacon sandwiches and hot drinks to over 500 walkers completing the 14-mile challenge. The walk, organised by Whitworth Sports Council, follows a circular route around the boundary of Whitworth, featuring moorland and varied terrain.

Diane Chadwick, a member of Thrum Hall Methodist Church, expressed satisfaction with the event, stating, "It was a glorious day, and the walkers seemed very pleased with our efforts." She added that the funds raised would support Christian Aid projects delivered by local partners in communities around the world.

The church plans to host another fundraiser, a pamper session with Afternoon Tea, on 26th July. Christian Aid reports that support from fundraisers helps reach vulnerable communities globally, having assisted 4.1 million people through nearly 400 projects between 2024 and 2025.
